explanation: Use 好不好 or 有没有 to ask whether something is the case. 如果 introduces a condition, so it is not used for these two indirect questions; 毒不毒 does not need 了 here.

before: 神农不知道他吃不吃灵芝或者夹竹桃
after: 神农不知道吃不吃灵芝或者夹竹桃
explanation: 神农 and 他 refer to the same person in the same sentence. When the subject stays the same, omit the repeated pronoun.

before: 别的人给了神农一个灵芝
after: 有一个人给了神农一个灵芝
explanation: 别的人 means people other than a person or group already mentioned, but there is no such person or group here. Introduce this new person with 有一个人.

before: 这个植物可以让神农更好
after: 这个植物可以让神农的身体更好
explanation: 说一个人更好 usually describes their character, not their health. Add 身体 to say that the plant improves Shennong's health.

before: 比方说，他会觉得更健康
after: 他会觉得更健康
explanation: 比方说 means “for example,” but this sentence is not giving an example. It directly states the result, so delete 比方说.

before: 吃灵芝以后
after: 吃了灵芝以后
explanation: Eating the lingzhi is completed before the later action of being able to walk again. Use 了 with 吃 to show that the eating has finished.

before: 最后，神农找到了很多植物，他可以用对药
after: 最后，神农找到了很多植物，可以用来做药
explanation: 神农 is already the subject in this sentence, so do not repeat 他. 用对药 is not a Chinese verb phrase; 用来做药 means “use them to make medicine.”

before: 别的人给了神农一个灵芝
after: 有人给了神农一个灵芝
explanation: 别的人 means “other people,” but it is not clear which group they are other than. Use 有人 to introduce an unspecified person here.

before: 比方说，他会觉得更健康
after: 他会觉得更健康
explanation: 比方说 means “for example,” but this sentence gives the result of taking the lingzhi, not an example. Delete it.

before: 神农找到了很多植物，他可以用对药
after: 神农找到了很多植物，可以用来做药
explanation: Use 用来做药 to say that plants can be used to make medicine. When 神农 is the subject of both parts of the same sentence, do not repeat it with 他.

before: 别的人给了神农一个灵芝
after: 有一些人给了神农一个灵芝
explanation: “别的人” means “other people,” but no group of people has been introduced for them to be “other” than. Introduce these new people as 有一些人.

before: 比方说，他会觉得更健康
after: 他会觉得更健康
explanation: 比方说 means “for example,” but this sentence is not giving an example. It simply explains that Shennong will feel healthier.

before: 吃灵芝以后
after: 吃了灵芝以后
explanation: Eating the lingzhi is finished before he can walk again, so 吃 needs 了.

before: 最后，神农找到了很多植物，他可以用对药
after: 最后，神农找到了很多可以用来治病的植物
explanation: 用对药 is not a correct way to say that plants are used as medicine. Say 可以用来治病, and place it before 植物 to describe the plants he found.

before: 他有一个问题，他不知道什么东西能做药
after: 他有一个问题，不知道什么东西能做药
explanation: The second 他 refers to 神农 again in the same sentence. After the subject has already been mentioned, omit the repeated pronoun.

before: 神农三个月走去
after: 神农走了三个月
explanation: A duration such as 三个月 comes after the action verb. Use 了 with 走 because the three-month journey was completed.

before: 找到有植物的地方
after: 找到了有植物的地方
explanation: Finding the place is a completed action in the story, so 找到 needs 了.

before: 他看到一个很漂亮的植物
after: 看到一株很漂亮的植物
explanation: Do not repeat 他 after 神农 in the same sentence. Also, use 株, not 个, as the measure word for a plant.

before: 但是，他有一个问题，他不知道什么东西能做药
after: 但是，他有一个问题，不知道什么东西能做药
explanation: 神农 is already the subject in this sentence, so do not repeat 他 before 不知道.

before: 什么病人吃都会觉得身体更好
after: 什么病人吃了都会觉得身体更好
explanation: Eating happens before the patient feels better, so 吃 needs 了 to show that this action is completed.

before: 神农三个月走去
after: 神农走了三个月
explanation: A duration such as 三个月 comes after the verb. Use 了 after 走 to show that the three-month journey was completed.

before: 他看到一个很漂亮的植物
after: 看到了一棵很漂亮的植物
explanation: 神农 is already the subject in the same sentence, so 他 is unnecessary. The final completed action needs 了, and the measure word for a plant is 棵, not 个.

before: 他有一个问题，他不知道什么东西能做药
after: 他有一个问题，不知道什么东西能做药
explanation: The subject is already 神农 in this sentence, so do not repeat 他. Chinese normally leaves out the repeated subject in the next clause.

before: 什么病人吃都会觉得身体更好
after: 什么病人吃了都会觉得身体更好
explanation: Eating happens before feeling better, so use 了 after 吃 to show that the eating is completed.

before: 神农三个月走去
after: 神农走了三个月
explanation: A duration such as 三个月 comes after the verb. Use 了 after 走 to show that he walked for three months.

before: 找到有植物的地方，他看到一个很漂亮的植物
after: 找到了有植物的地方，看到一株很漂亮的植物
explanation: The subject is still 神农, so do not repeat 他 in the same sentence. Use 了 for the completed action 找到, and use 株, not 个, for a plant.

before: 这种一定是做药的花
after: 这种花一定是做药的
explanation: 这种 needs a noun after it here: 这种花 means “this kind of flower.” Put the noun before 一定是, and use 做药的 as the description of the flower.

before: 吃了以后，神农快生病
after: 吃了以后，神农很快生病了
explanation: 很快 means that the action happened soon. Use 了 because getting sick is a completed event in the story.

before: 快给他一种红的灵芝
after: 很快给了他一种红的灵芝
explanation: Use 很快, not 快, to mean “quickly” in this statement. Give the last verb in this completed series of actions the particle 了.

before: 神农吃了以后，他没有病，想起来以前一个人告诉他，灵芝对身体有好处
after: 神农吃了以后，没有病了，然后想起以前有一个人告诉他，灵芝对身体有好处
explanation: Do not repeat 他 in the same sentence when it refers to 神农; the subject can be omitted. Use 了 for the changed state, 然后 to connect the next event, and 有一个人 to introduce a person for the first time.

before: 神农快生病
after: 神农生病了
explanation: 快 means “soon” or “about to,” but the story says that he became ill after eating the flower. Use 了 for the completed action.

before: 一个穿着蓝色衣服的人帮神农，快给他一种红的灵芝
after: 一个穿着蓝色衣服的人帮神农，很快给了他一种红的灵芝
explanation: This is a completed past action, so 给 needs 了. 很快 means “very quickly” in a narrative; 快给 can sound like an order to “give quickly.”

before: 神农吃了以后，他没有病
after: 神农吃了以后，没有病
explanation: When the subject is the same within one sentence, Chinese normally omits the repeated pronoun. 神农 is already the subject, so do not add 他.

before: 想起来以前一个人告诉他，灵芝对身体有好处
after: 想起了以前一个人告诉他灵芝对身体有好处
explanation: Remembering is a completed action here, so use 了 after 想起. The words being remembered can follow directly without a comma.

before: 神农快生病
after: 神农很快生病了
explanation: This is a completed event in the story, so 生病 needs 了. 很快 means “very soon” or “quickly”; 快 alone here does not mean that.

before: 帮神农，快给他一种红的灵芝
after: 帮神农，很快给了他一种红的灵芝
explanation: 快给 can sound like an order to “give quickly.” Use 很快 for a narrative event, and use 了 on the final verb of this completed series of actions.

before: 神农吃了以后，他没有病
after: 神农吃了以后，没有病
explanation: 神农 and 他 refer to the same person in the same sentence. After naming the subject, Chinese normally leaves out the repeated pronoun.

before: 想起来以前一个人告诉他，灵芝对身体有好处
after: 想起了以前有一个人告诉他，灵芝对身体有好处
explanation: Remembering is a completed action here, so use 想起了. Say 以前有一个人 to introduce that person in the past.

before: 他找到药以后他写下怎么做药在书上
after: 他找到药以后，在书上写下了怎么做药
explanation: A place phrase with 在 comes before the verb in Chinese, so say 在书上写下. Since the writing was completed, 写下 takes 了.

before: 那红灵芝对身体好处
after: 那种红灵芝对身体有好处
explanation: Use a measure word such as 种 after 那 when referring to a type of 灵芝. 好处 needs 有 here: 对身体有好处 means “to be good for the body.”

before: 一回家就告诉别人
after: 一回家就告诉了别人
explanation: This is one completed action in the story, so 告诉 needs 了.

before: 他找到药以后他写下怎么做药在书上
after: 他找到药以后，把怎么做药写在书上了
explanation: After 他 has already introduced the subject at the start of this sentence, do not repeat 他. Use 把 to put the thing being written before 写在书上, and use 了 for the completed writing action.

before: 那红灵芝对身体好处
after: 那种红灵芝对身体有好处
explanation: A demonstrative such as 那 needs a measure word before this noun; 那种 is appropriate for a kind of lingzhi. The fixed phrase is 对身体有好处, with 有.

before: 他把灵芝放在包里
after: 他把灵芝放在包里了
explanation: Putting the lingzhi in the bag is a completed action in the story, so it needs 了.

before: 他找到药以后他写下怎么做药在书上
after: 他找到药以后，在书上写下了怎么做药
explanation: Do not repeat 他 in the same sentence when it has the same subject. 在书上 comes before 写下, and the completed action 写下 needs 了.

before: 那红灵芝对身体好处
after: 那红灵芝对身体有好处
explanation: Use 有好处 to say that something is good for the body.

before: 古代的时候
after: 在古代
explanation: Use 在古代 to say “in ancient times.” 古代的时候 is not the usual expression here.

before: 什么植物能吃，什么植物不能吃
after: 什么植物是能吃的，什么植物是不能吃的
explanation: When saying which plants are edible and which are not, use 是能吃的 and 是不能吃的.

before: 因为他们吃了毒
after: 因为他们吃的植物有毒
explanation: The intended meaning is that the plants they ate were poisonous. Say that the plants have poison, rather than saying they ate poison.

before: 有一个老人叫神农，他什么植物都觉得好吃
after: 有一个老人叫神农，觉得什么植物都好吃
explanation: 神农 is introduced in this same sentence, so do not repeat him with 他. Chinese can leave the subject out here.

before: 他们还怕吃毒
after: 他们还怕中毒
explanation: 中毒 means “to be poisoned.” 怕吃毒 does not express the intended meaning naturally.

before: 古代的时候
after: 在古代
explanation: Use 在古代 to say that something happened in ancient times. 古代的时候 is not the usual expression here.

before: 什么植物能吃，什么植物不能吃
after: 什么植物是能吃的，什么植物是不能吃的
explanation: When contrasting which plants are edible and which are not, use 是能吃的 and 是不能吃的.

before: 他们吃了毒
after: 他们吃了有毒的植物
explanation: 毒 by itself is not the thing the people ate here. Say that they ate poisonous plants.

before: 有一个老人叫神农，他什么植物都觉得好吃
after: 有一个老人叫神农，什么植物都觉得好吃
explanation: After introducing 神农 in the same sentence, omit the repeated subject pronoun. The omitted subject still clearly refers to 神农.

before: 如果他们还怕吃毒，不会吃他喜欢的植物
after: 如果他们还怕吃有毒的植物，就不会吃他喜欢的植物
explanation: Say 吃有毒的植物 rather than 吃毒. With 如果, use 就 in the result clause to show the condition and its result.

before: 古代的时候
after: 在古代
explanation: Use 在古代 to say “in ancient times.” 古代的时候 is not the usual expression here.

before: 因为他们吃了毒
after: 因为他们吃的植物有毒
explanation: The problem is that the plants were poisonous, not that the people intentionally ate poison. Say that the plants they ate had poison.

before: 有一个老人叫神农，他什么植物都觉得好吃
after: 有一个老人叫神农，什么植物都觉得好吃
explanation: After introducing 神农 in the same sentence, leave out the repeated pronoun. The omitted subject still clearly refers to 神农.

before: 如果他们还怕吃毒，不会吃他喜欢的植物
after: 如果他们还怕中毒，就不会吃他喜欢的植物
explanation: 怕中毒 means “be afraid of being poisoned.” With 如果, use 就 in the result part of the conditional sentence.

before: 吃了很多样子的植物
after: 吃了很多种植物
explanation: 样子 means appearance. Use 种 to count different kinds of plants.

before: 他是第一人，找到了茶
after: 他是第一个找到茶的人
explanation: To say someone was the first person to do an action, use 第一个 + verb + 的人.

before: 他一直都吃了
after: 他一直都在吃
explanation: 一直 describes an action continuing over time, so use 在 to show the ongoing action. Do not use 了 here.

before: 他连毒都能吃
after: 连毒都能吃
explanation: The subject 他 has already appeared in the same sentence, so Chinese normally leaves it out in the next clause.

before: 可是他还没吃了一个叫夹竹桃的植物
after: 可是他还没吃过一种叫夹竹桃的植物
explanation: 了 cannot be used after 没. Use 没吃过 to say that he had not tried it, and use 种 for a kind of plant.

before: 找到了那个像星星的植物
after: 找到那个像星星的植物
explanation: In this series of actions, only the final action takes 了. The final verb 吃下了 already shows that the actions were completed.

before: 吃了很多样子的植物
after: 吃了很多种植物
explanation: Use 种, not 样子, to count different kinds of plants. 样子 means an appearance or shape.

before: 他是第一人，找到了茶
after: 他是第一个找到茶的人
explanation: Use 第一个……的人 to say that someone was the first person to do an action. 第一人 is not a natural way to express this meaning.

before: 他一直都吃了
after: 他一直都在吃
explanation: 一直 describes an ongoing action, so use 在 with the dynamic verb 吃. Do not use 了 for an action that is continuing.

before: 他连毒都能吃
after: 他连有毒的植物都能吃
explanation: 毒 is poison, not the plant that he eats. Say 有毒的植物 for poisonous plants.

before: 他还没吃了一个叫夹竹桃的植物
after: 他还没吃过一个叫夹竹桃的植物
explanation: Do not use 了 after 没. Use 过 here because the sentence says that he has not had the experience of eating this plant.

before: 他找到了那个像星星的植物，觉得很漂亮，马上就吃下了
after: 他找到那个像星星的植物，觉得很漂亮，马上就吃下了
explanation: In a series of completed actions, only the last verb takes 了. Here, 吃下了 is the last action, so 找到 does not need 了.

before: 吃了很多样子的植物
after: 尝试了很多种植物
explanation: 很多样子 describes appearances, not different kinds. Use 很多种植物 for many kinds of plants; 尝试 is the suitable verb for trying plants.

before: 他是第一人，找到了茶
after: 他是第一个找到茶的人
explanation: To say someone is the first person who did something, use 第一个 followed by the action and 的人.

before: 他一直都吃了
after: 他一直都吃
explanation: 一直 describes a habitual or continuing action here, so it does not take the completion marker 了.

before: 他连毒都能吃
after: 他连有毒的植物都能吃
explanation: 毒 means poison itself. Here the story means poisonous plants, so say 有毒的植物.

before: 可是他还没吃了一个叫夹竹桃的植物
after: 可是他还没吃过一种叫夹竹桃的植物
explanation: After 没, do not use 了. Use 过 to say he has not had the experience of eating it, and use 种 as the measure word for a kind of plant.

before: 觉得他快会死了
after: 觉得快要死了
explanation: The person who feels this is also the person who is about to die, so do not repeat 他 here. Use 快要 to say that something is about to happen.

before: 正好有别人找到他了
after: 正好有人找到他
explanation: Use 有人 for an unspecified person. 别人 means “other people” and needs a clear group that they are other than.

before: 他吃灵芝以后就觉得很好
after: 他吃了灵芝以后就觉得很好
explanation: The eating is completed before the later feeling, so use 了 with 吃 before 以后.

before: 像星星的植物是毒
after: 像星星的植物有毒
explanation: Use 有毒 to say that a plant is poisonous. 是毒 is not the usual way to express this.

before: 他快会死了
after: 他快要死了
explanation: Use 快要 or 快 before a verb to say that something will happen very soon. 快会 is not used this way.

before: 正好有别人找到他了，给了他一个像伞的植物
after: 正好有人找到他，给了他一个像伞的植物
explanation: Use 有人 to introduce an unknown person; 别人 means other people. In a series of completed actions, only the last verb takes 了, so 找到 does not need 了 here.

before: 吃灵芝以后
after: 吃了灵芝以后
explanation: Eating the lingzhi is completed before the next event, so use 了 with 吃.

before: 像星星的植物是毒
after: 像星星的植物有毒
explanation: Say a plant 有毒 to mean that it is poisonous. 是毒 is not the usual way to describe a poisonous plant.

before: 他在地上躺着，觉得他快会死了
after: 他在地上躺着，觉得自己快要死了
explanation: When the person who feels something and the person in the thought are the same, use 自己. Say 快要死了 for something that is about to happen; 快会死 is not natural here.

before: 可是正好有别人找到他了，给了他一个像伞的植物
after: 可是正好有一个人找到他，给了他一个像伞的植物
explanation: 别人 means “other people” and is unclear because no person has been introduced here. Introduce this new character as 有一个人. In this series of actions, only the last verb takes 了.

before: 吃灵芝以后
after: 吃了灵芝以后
explanation: Eating the lingzhi is finished before he feels better, so use 了 after 吃.

before: 他测量起来了
after: 他明白了
explanation: 测量 means “to measure,” which does not fit this meaning. He understands the effects of the two plants, so use 明白了.

before: 像星星的植物是毒
after: 像星星的植物有毒
explanation: Use 有毒 to say that a plant is poisonous. 是毒 means that the plant itself is poison.
